lines: כָּל־הַבָּא אֵלָיו יָשִׂיג יְשׁוּעָה וְיֵלֵךְ וְיָעִיד

review: 4:1 טַעֲמוּ וּרְאוּ — Psalm 34:9 (טַעֲמוּ וּרְאוּ כִּי־טוֹב יְהוָה); the Arabic ذُوقُوهُ وَانْظُرُوا is the psalm's own invitation, and the Hebrew keeps the two imperatives rather than a single 'experience'.

4:3 מַה־טּוֹב אֲדֹנָי — Psalm 34:9 again, now as the answer the invitation promises; the Arabic مَا أَطْيَبَ الرَّبَّ الْإلٰه is that exclamation, and the Hebrew casts it as the psalm's clause so the stanza closes on the verse it opened with.

1:4 מִיּוֹם מוֹלַדְתִּי הֶחָדָשׁ — the Arabic مِنْ يَوْمِ مَوْلِدِي الْجَدِيد is 'from the day of my new birth'; the glossary noun מוֹלֶדֶת is kept so the line says birth, not the Modern Hebrew לֵדָה.
3:4 אֶרְדֹּף אֶת־עִקְּבוֹתֶיךָ — the Arabic أَقْتَفِي خُطَاك is 'I follow Your steps'; the Hebrew keeps the concrete footprints (עִקְּבוֹת, as in Song 1:8) rather than the abstract 'walk'.

2:4 וַיְפַתְּחֵנִי — Job 39:5 (יְפַתֵּחַ) and Ps 116:16 (פִּתַּחְתָּ); the Arabic فَكَّنِي is 'He loosed my fetters', and the Hebrew keeps the verb of unfastening chains rather than the general 'freed'.
